text: Partial/lazy graph rendering (dotted stubs, load on click)
description: General capability (also valuable for large single repos): support graphs too big to fully load. Unloaded aims render as dotted-outline stubs with no loaded info. Clicking a stub loads the aim and reveals its relatives as new dotted stubs. The store holds a mix of loaded aims and stubs; value calc treats stubs as boundary leaves. This is the substrate cross-repo rendering builds on (externals are just stubs from another repo).

status.comment: Phase-filter graphs now render ring-only loadable nodes and expand them on click, but these are projections of aims already loaded in the client. True storage/network-level lazy loading, mixed loaded/stub value calculation, and incremental relative discovery remain unimplemented. Defer that architecture until measured graph scale demonstrates the need.

reflection: Relevance reconciliation on 24 July 2026 found a useful UI slice in graph-store/useGraphSimulation/WebGLGraphRenderer: phase filtering creates loadable boundary nodes, ring-renders them, and expands relatives on click. This does not satisfy the original performance/storage claim because dataStore still holds full aims. Avoid broadening it without a benchmark; optimize measured bottlenecks first.
